claims.reason: The two lemmas do have the same overall shape, but the repeated reasoning is not substantial enough for the rubric. (1) The `ext; ring` rewrite is a one-line algebraic identity, i.e. a short calculation. (2) The proposed shared lemma `deriv_qaryEntropy_eq_add_of_mem_Ioo` is `deriv_qaryEntropy` plus `ring`, with `p ≠ 0` and `p ≠ 1` read off `Ioo 0 1`. That is a thin wrapper around existing API, and `deriv_qaryEntropy` already holds the real content (the derivative formula). (3) The `filter_upwards … Tendsto.congr'` step and the `not_continuousAt_of_tendsto … nhdsWithin_le_nhds` call with a `disjoint_nhds_at…_iff` side goal are plumbing around existing Mathlib lemmas. They are also not literally identical: one side uses `𝓝[<] 1`, `atBot` and `Ioo_mem_nhdsLT`, the other `𝓝[>] 0`, `atTop` and `Ioo_mem_nhdsGT`. The mathematical work is already factored into the two private tendsto lemmas. The only duplication left is mirrored filter-level boilerplate. Merging it would be tidying (moving duplicated branches into a helper), not removal of non-trivial repeated proof machinery. In the rewritten `one` case, the proposed membership proof `⟨by linarith [hp.1], hp.2⟩` also needs the numeral fact `0 < 1 - 2⁻¹`. This is plausible but untested. The saving is only a few lines in each proof.
claims.shared_lemma: private lemma deriv_qaryEntropy_eq_add_of_mem_Ioo (hp : p ∈ Ioo (0:ℝ) 1) : deriv (qaryEntropy q) p = log (q - 1) + (log (1 - p) - log p)  -- proof: deriv_qaryEntropy hp.1.ne' hp.2.ne, then ring. This is only a thin wrapper, so it is not accepted as a confirmed refactor.
